rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Change temperature while retaining the scouting gradient to probe selectivity in the crowded central cluster. The substantial time margin allows subsequent slope refinement if temperature alone does not resolve the critical pairs.

Probe the low-temperature end while keeping the gradient fixed, since heating improved one central separation but introduced another critical pair. This establishes whether cooling offers a better selectivity window before refining gradient slope.

Test an intermediate warm temperature with a shallower gradient to spread the central cluster while avoiding the near-coelution seen at 55 C. The current elution-time margin should accommodate the longer gradient without a time penalty.

Raise temperature one step at the shallower gradient to improve the remaining central critical pair. The increased separation earlier in the cluster may now accommodate 55 C without recreating the bottleneck from injection 2.
Injection 5 achieved the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to test whether full resolution can be retained with faster elution.

Reduce the endpoint to make the 12-minute gradient slightly steeper than the fully resolved benchmark but shallower than injection 6. This should recover the critical separation while modestly shortening elution relative to injection 5.

Test a lower starting organic fraction to alter selectivity in the central cluster, paired with a steeper gradient to accelerate late elution. Injection 7 remains the fully resolved benchmark if this faster method sacrifices resolution.

Test a faster gradient at the highest temperature to seek a different selectivity window after possible central peak-order changes. Injection 8 already achieves maximum CRF, so this run explores whether comparable resolution is possible with substantially faster elution.

Raise the starting organic fraction to test whether the central near-coelution at 60 C separates on the reversed-order side while retaining rapid elution. All other pairs in injection 9 had resolution above 1.5, making this a promising alternative selectivity window.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction further improves the reversed central separation seen in injection 10. A slightly longer gradient should help protect neighboring separations, while checking whether the earliest peaks remain sufficiently retained.

Shorten injection 10’s gradient to test whether the reversed central pair separates further at higher slope. This probes the fast-method boundary, with the adjacent central separation likely to become limiting.

Explore a higher starting organic fraction at moderate temperature to seek an alternative central-cluster selectivity pattern without the severe early-peak compression seen at 60 C. The maximum-score method from injection 8 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Return to the fastest fully resolved method, injection 8, and increase the endpoint by one grid step. This tests whether a modest slope increase can shorten elution while preserving its two marginal central separations.

Probe the untested temperature between 25 and 40 C for an alternative central-peak ordering that could support faster full resolution. Injection 8 remains the fastest maximum-score method; its slope limit is now bracketed by injection 14.

Test a steeper gradient at an untested intermediate temperature to determine whether slope-driven selectivity opens a faster separation window. Keep injection 8 as the fastest fully resolved benchmark, since increasing its slope already reduced CRF.

Refine the successful 55 C window with a slope between injections 6 and 7, targeting full resolution with earlier elution than injection 7. This may also provide a better minimum-resolution margin than the fastest fully resolved method, injection 8.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower slope to preserve the critical central separation while reducing initial retention. This refines the established maximum-score temperature window rather than revisiting the less successful temperature extremes.

Flatten the gradient from injection 18 to recover its only unresolved pair while retaining the improved separation later in the cluster. This tests for a maximum-score alternative with a larger resolution margin, though injection 8 remains the speed benchmark.

Increase the endpoint one step from injection 19 to shorten elution while using its resolution margin. This should retain full resolution with more margin at the weakest pair than the fastest maximum-score method, injection 8.

Narrow injection 8’s gradient window while preserving its slope, so the predicted last peak at 7.60 minutes still precedes the gradient’s arrival at its final composition at the outlet. This tests a shorter programmed gradient expected to retain maximum CRF and full resolution.

Test whether a shallower gradient at 60 C restores the central separation that limited the faster high-temperature runs. The low starting organic fraction should protect early resolution, while the last peak is expected to remain near or below 10 minutes.

Test a small slope increase over injection 17 to locate the full-resolution boundary more precisely. The critical pair may fall just below 1.5; injections 8 and 21 remain the fastest demonstrated maximum-score methods.

Use a slope between the fully resolved injections 19 and 20, targeting balanced margins at the two critical pairs. The narrower gradient window should preserve maximum CRF with the last peak below 10 minutes; injections 8 and 21 remain the fastest fully resolved options.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving injection 21’s slope through the critical central cluster, then hold at 50% organic to elute the isolated last peak. This tests a narrower maximum-score method; injections 8 and 21 remain the fastest demonstrated fully resolved options.
